item.title: Joint Statement on the Conviction of Hong Kong Alliance Leaders and Sentencing of Joshua Wong
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the Conviction of Hong Kong Alliance Leaders and Sentencing of Joshua Wong

Media Note

November 6, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by Governments of the United States of America, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. 

Begin Text.

Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment following a further charge under the National Security Law (NSL).  This comes just months after leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance were convicted under the same legislation. These are further examples of how the NSL is being used to target individuals for political expression and participation.  We call for an immediate end to all unjust prosecutions of individuals charged under the NSL and urge the authorities in China and Hong Kong to uphold their international commitments and honor the rights and freedoms guaranteed to the people of Hong Kong under the Sino-British Joint Declaration (1984).

 End Text.

item.title: Reward Offers Totaling Up to $50 Million for Information Leading to Arrests and/or Convictions of Leaders of Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Reward Offers Totaling Up to $50 Million for Information Leading to Arrests and/or Convictions of Leaders of Foreign Terrorist Organization Tren de Aragua

Press Statement

November 5, 2026

Today, the Department of State’s Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs, in coordination with the FBI, DEA, and Department of Justice, is announcing new and increased reward offers totaling up to $50 million under the Transnational Organized Crime Rewards Program (TOCRP) for information leading to the arrests and/or convictions of the top three leaders of Tren de Aragua (TdA), a violent Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) designated by the Trump Administration last year. 

  • Yohan José Romero, a.k.a. “Yohan Petrica”: reward offer increase from up to $4 million to up to $20 million; 
  • Giovanni Vicente Mosquera Serrano, a.k.a. “Giovanni” and “El Viejo”: reward offer increase from up to $5 million to up to $15 million; and 
  • Juan Gabriel Rivas Núñez , a.k.a. “Juancho”: new reward offer of up to $15 million. 

According to court documents, Romero is the current leader of TdA and directs the group’s operations, including narcotrafficking, illegal gold mining in Venezuela, and murders.  Mosquera Serrano and Rivas Núñez are both second-in-command to Romero, with Mosquera Serrano overseeing TdA operations in the United States, Colombia, and Central America, while Rivas Núñez oversees TdA operations in Venezuela.  Mosquera Serrano also is one of the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives and has directed multiple acts of violence involving robbery, extortion, and kidnapping. 

On July 29, 2026, a superseding indictment filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas charged Romero, Mosquera Serrano, and Rivas Núñez with conspiracy to provide, providing, and attempting to provide material support to an FTO.  Mosquera Serrano was also charged with international cocaine distribution and international cocaine distribution conspiracy.   

Today’s reward offers are authorized by the Assistant Secretary for International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs under the TOCRP, which supports law enforcement efforts to disrupt transnational crime globally.  If you have information, please contact the FBI at +1-281-787-9939 (phone/text/WhatsApp/Telegram).  If you are located outside of the United States, you may also contact the nearest U.S. embassy or consulate.  If you are in the United States, you may also contact the local FBI office in your city. 

ALL IDENTITIES ARE KEPT STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL.  Government officials and employees are not eligible for rewards based on information provided in the course of official duty.

item.title: Dismantling the Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Dismantling the Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization

Press Statement

November 5, 2026

Today, the United States is sanctioning four individuals and 41 entities linked to the Cambodia-based Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO), building on the October 2025 and June 2026 designations targeting the organization’s leadership, affiliated companies, and financial facilitators.  These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).   

Prince Group TCO members target victims in the United States and around the world through sophisticated cyber-enabled fraud schemes, many of which are carried out from large-scale scam compounds in Southeast Asia.  Today’s designations target several individuals and affiliated companies who continue to provide material support to the Prince Group TCO.   

Additionally, the United States is sanctioning Chui Kok Wa, a Malaysian individual who defrauded U.S. victims by managing a network of scammers located in Madagascar.  This network perpetrated scams targeting Americans, including schemes to defraud them of digital assets.  On October 27, 2026, charges were unsealed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia charging Chui with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. 

No criminal network is beyond reach. The Trump Administration will continue to expose, sanction, and dismantle the criminal networks that prey on Americans through cybercrime, fraud, and extortion. 

Today’s actions were taken in furtherance of Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens” and pursuant to E.O. 13581 “Blocking Property of Transnational Criminal Organizations,” as amended by E.O. 13863, and E.O. 13694 “Blocking the Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities,” as further amended. 

For more information about today’s actions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Further Sanctions on the Cuban Regime’s Foreign Military Support and Illicit Revenue Networks
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Further Sanctions on the Cuban Regime’s Foreign Military Support and Illicit Revenue Networks 

Press Statement

November 5, 2026

Cuba’s ruling elite is hoarding the island’s energy, shipping, and technology resources for its own enrichment, leaving the Cuban people to contend with blackouts, shortages, and a stagnant economy.  The Marxist regime in Havana relies on a web of state-owned enterprises, joint ventures, and offshore intermediaries to keep this system running; its foreign backers supply the military equipment that helps sustain the regime’s military forces and enable its brutal repression, while propping up its persistent efforts to threaten, infiltrate and subvert the American homeland. 

Today, pursuant to President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to United States National Security and Foreign Policy,” I am designating ten targets including additional Cuban elites, a crude oil shipping network, state-owned import and technical-support entities, and China-based suppliers of the regime’s military forces.  I am also identifying five associated vessels as blocked property. 

Among today’s targets is GUILLERMO FAUSTINO RODRIGUEZ LOPEZ CALLEJA, who is part of an extensive web of offshore shipping companies that move Cuban crude oil shipments to and from the island.  I am also designating ANY RODRIGUEZ LASTRES, daughter of the previously designated Grupo de Administración Empresarial (GAESA) President Ania Guillermina Lastres Morera. 

Additionally, the Department of the Treasury issued a determination pursuant to E.O. 14404 that authorizes the imposition of economic sanctions on any foreign person operating or having operated in the electronics, manufacturing, marine, and technology sectors of the Cuban economy. 

The Trump Administration will not stand by while the Cuban regime funnels the island’s resources to its military elite, while regime insiders and their family members profit from opaque offshore networks, and while Cuba continues to serve as a staging ground for a global coalition of hostile anti-American actors to threaten, spy on, and plot against the United States and its interests.  

The Department’s actions are being taken pursuant to E.O. 14404, which authorizes sweeping sanctions on Cuba, including against persons who support the Cuban regime’s security apparatus and those responsible for repression in Cuba and other threats to U.S. national security.  These actions also further both E.O. 14380, Addressing Threats to the United States by the Government of Cuba and National Security Presidential Memorandum 5, which directs the Executive Branch to improve human rights, encourage the rule of law, foster free markets and free enterprise, and promote democracy in Cuba.  For more information on today’s action, see the Department of State’s Fact Sheet.

item.title: Disrupting Iran’s Pursuit of Man-Portable Air-Defense Systems
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

Disrupting Iran’s Pursuit of Man-Portable Air-Defense Systems

Press Statement

November 4, 2026

Today, the Department of State is imposing sanctions on two individuals and one entity based in Belarus, Russia, and Nigeria, respectively, for their involvement in the Iranian regime’s efforts to procure man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS).

Consistent with Operation Economic Outcast, this is the latest in a series of U.S. actions against Iran’s military procurement networks involving MANPADS.  It follows designations on May 8, June 10, and July 15, 2026.  Each round makes it harder and more costly for Tehran to arm itself and reinforces the UN restrictions restored in September 2025.

Iran’s procurement efforts threaten U.S. national security, and the United States will take all necessary action to hold the Iranian regime accountable.  

The United States will continue to work with partners to implement the restored UN measures and to stop the flow of weapons that threaten U.S. forces and regional security.  Anyone who helps the regime build its arsenal should expect to be held accountable.

The Department of State’s action was taken pursuant to E.O. 13949, which targets certain persons with respect to the conventional arms activities of Iran.  For more information about today’s actions, see the Department of State’s fact sheet.

item.title: Disrupting Iran’s Pursuit of Man-Portable Air-Defense Systems Fact Sheet
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Disrupting Iran’s Pursuit of Man-Portable Air-Defense Systems Fact Sheet

Fact Sheet

November 4, 2026

Today, the Department of State is designating two individuals and one entity that have been involved in efforts to help the Iranian regime obtain man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS). 

These designations continue a sustained U.S. campaign against Iran’s military procurement networks involving MANPADS.  They follow actions on May 8, June 10, and July 15, 2026.  Together, these actions close off more of the channels Tehran uses to try to rebuild its arsenal and raise the risk for third-country brokers and suppliers.  Today’s action also supports enforcement of the UN arms embargo on Iran restored in September 2025.  Those restrictions bar UN Member States from supplying such weapons to Iran.

The United States will keep exposing the networks that arm Iran’s military and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and will keep denying the regime the resources that sustain its destabilizing activities.

All three targets are being designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13949, which targets certain persons with respect to the conventional arms activities of Iran. Designations Pursuant to Section 1(a)(iii) of E.O. 13949

  • (U) MOHAMMED ALI TOLIBOV (TOLIBOV) is the Chief Executive Officer of Armory Alliance and has contributed to Armory Alliance’s efforts to procure weapons on behalf of Iran.  Armory Alliance is a Belarus-based entity that has acted as an intermediary between China-based companies and Iran and has been involved in efforts to facilitate the purchase of hundreds of MANPADS.  Armory Alliance was previously designated pursuant to E.O. 13382 and E.O. 13949.   TOLIBOV was previously designated under E.O. 13382. 
  • (U) VANGUARD TACTICAL SUPPLY LIMITED (VANGUARD) is a Nigeria-based entity that has been involved in efforts to facilitate the procurement of Chinese-origin MANPADS for Iran via false end-users.  VANGUARD was previously designated under E.O. 13382.
  • (U) ALISHER DOMULLODZHANOV (DOMULLODZHANOV) is a Russia-based individual who has been involved in efforts to facilitate the procurement of MANPADS for Iran.  

Sanctions Implications 

As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 13949, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to the Department of Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).  In addition, all entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. 

All transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt.  These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. 

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law. 

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be sent to: OFAC.Reconsideration@treasury.gov.  Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

item.title: Further Sanctions on the Cuban Regime’s Foreign Military Support and Illicit Revenue Networks – Fact Sheet
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Further Sanctions on the Cuban Regime’s Foreign Military Support and Illicit Revenue Networks – Fact Sheet

Fact Sheet

November 5, 2026

Today, the Department of State is designating eight entities and two individuals, and identifying five vessels as blocked property, to further the Trump Administration’s comprehensive push to end the Cuban regime’s malign activities, both in Cuba and across our hemisphere.  This action includes targets associated with the Cuban regime’s oil shipping networks, Cuban elites, state-owned import and technical-support entities, and China-based suppliers of the regime’s military forces.   

All Department of State targets sanctioned today have been designated pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14404, which authorizes sanctions on foreign persons determined to meet specified criteria related to repression in Cuba and other threats to U.S. national security and foreign policy. 

Additionally, today the Director of the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a determination pursuant to E.O. 14404 that authorizes sanctions against any foreign person operating or having operated in the manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine sectors of the Cuban economy.  The identification of these new sectors targets the regime and those who enable it, not the Cuban people.  The United States continues to authorize humanitarian trade, including food, medicine, and medical devices, and supports the free flow of information to the Cuban people.

Cuban Regime’s Illicit Revenue Networks 

Cuba’s ruling elite hoards the island’s energy and shipping resources for its own enrichment, leaving the Cuban people to contend with blackouts, fuel shortages, and a stagnant economy.  To keep this system running, the regime relies on a web of offshore intermediaries.  Today, the Department of State is designating part of an extensive shipping network moving crude oil and petroleum products for the Cuban regime.  

  • GUILLERMO FAUSTINO RODRIGUEZ LOPEZ CALLEJA (GUILLERMO) is part of an extensive network of maritime shipping companies moving petroleum products to and from Cuba.  GUILLERMO is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. 
  • CAROIL TRANSPORT MARINE LTD (CAROIL), a Cyprus-based company that manages Cuban-flagged crude oil tankers that have transported energy products in Cuba.  Treasury previously designated CAROIL on September 24, 2019, pursuant to E.O. 13850.  CAROIL is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy.  The following vessels are being identified as property in which CAROIL has an interest: 
  • ESPERANZA (IMO: 9289166): CAROIL is the commercial manager.  Treasury previously identified ESPERANZA as blocked property of CAROIL on December 3, 2019. 
  • GLORIA C (IMO: 9540273): CAROIL is the commercial manager.  TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC, is the registered owner. 
  • MARIA CRISTINA (IMO: 9502453): CAROIL is the commercial manager and registered owner.  Treasury previously identified MARIA CRISTINA as blocked property of CAROIL on September 24, 2019.  
  • TENTACOOL COMMERCIAL INC (TENTACOOL), a Panama-based company and the registered owner of the GLORIA C. TENTACOOL is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy. 
  • INTERNACIONAL MARITIMA SA, a Cuba-based company and the registered owner of the ESPERANZA.  INTERNACIONAL MARITIMA SA is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy.   
  • PETROLEOS MARITIMOS DEL CARIBE S.A. (PETROMARCA), a Cuba-based company and the ship manager and operator of two Cuban-flagged petroleum product tankers.  PETROMARCA is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(A) of E.O. 14404 for operating in or having operated in the energy sector of the Cuban economy.  The following vessels are being identified as property in which PETROMARCA has an interest: 
  • EMILIA (IMO: 9242209):  PETROMARCA is the commercial manager and registered owner.   
  • LOURDES (IMO: 9259692):  PETROMARCA is the commercial manager. 

Cuban Elites

Regime insiders and their family members continue to profit from the Cuban regime’s control of the island’s economy, including through opaque networks tied to Grupo De Administracion Empresarial S.A. (GAESA), the Cuban military’s business conglomerate.  Today, the Department of State is designating the daughter of the previously designated GAESA President.  

  • ANY RODRIGUEZ LASTRES (LASTRES), the daughter of the sanctioned GAESA President Ania Guillermina Lastres Morera.  LASTRES is being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(I) of E.O. 14404 for being an adult family member of ANIA GUILLERMINA LASTRES MORERA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to this order.  LASTRES also previously served as the Commercial Director of U.S.-designated Terminal De Contenedores De Mariel S.A. 

State-Owned Entities of the Cuban Regime 

The Cuban regime relies on a web of state-owned enterprises that control the island’s technology resources and direct revenue to the state rather than to the Cuban people.  Today, the Department of State is designating the following two Cuban state-owned entities pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(B) of E.O. 14404 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Government of Cuba.   

  • EMPRESA IMPORTADORA Y EXPORTADORA DE PRODUCTOS DE LA ELECTRONICA Y LAS COMUNICACIONES (CUBAELECTRONICA), a Cuban state-owned importer of supplies and equipment for Cuba’s electronics industry.  
  • EMPRESA COMERCIALIZADORA DE SERVICIOS TECNICOS Y TECNOLOGICOS (TECNOSIME), a Cuban state-owned entity that conducts commercial, labor, and promotional activities that generate revenue for the Cuban state.

Chinese Companies’ Support to the Cuban Military  

As the Department’s July 20 report Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism noted, the Cuban regime’s continuing partnerships with China and Russia have supplied Cuba with military hardware, surveillance technologies, and other security capabilities.  Today, the Department of State is taking aim at Cuba’s foreign backers by designating two China-based corporations that have supplied the Cuban regime with components and equipment to sustain the Cuban military.  The transfer of this equipment involved the Cuban company Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A., which was designated by the Department of State on August 6, 2026, and has been involved in the import of military-related equipment from China and Russia to Cuba. 

The following entities are being designated pursuant to Sec. 2(a)(i)(D) of E.O. 14404 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of Cuba.

  • CHINA NATIONAL ELECTRONIC IMPORT AND EXPORT COMPANY (CEIEC), a China-based state-owned enterprise that exports defense electronics, security systems, and construction engineering services.  Additionally, CEIEC contracted with the Cuban arms procurement entity Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A. to export components intended for military equipment used by the Cuban Ministry of Revolutionary Armed Forces (MINFAR) in 2026.  CEIEC was previously designated by the Department of the Treasury pursuant to E.O. 13692 on November 30, 2020, in relation to its support for the Maduro regime’s efforts to restrict internet service and conduct digital surveillance and cyber operations against political opponents.  
  • BEIJING H&C TECHNOLOGIES CO., LTD, a China-based subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC) International Co., Ltd. (CETCI) that sells surveillance and security equipment.  Additionally, BEIJING H&C TECHNOLOGIES CO., LTD worked with the Cuban arms procurement entity Sociedad Mercantil Duna S.A. to export military equipment to Cuba in 2026. 

Sanctions Implications  

As a result of today’s sanctions actions, and in accordance with E.O. 14404 of May 1, 2026, “Imposing Sanctions on Those Responsible for Repression in Cuba and for Threats to U.S. National Security and Foreign Policy,” all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  Additionally, all entities that are owned individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked. 

All transactions and dealings by U.S. persons or persons within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons are prohibited unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC or exempt.  These prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any blocked person and the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Foreign persons that engage in transactions with persons designated pursuant to E.O. 14404—or that operate or have operated in the electronics, energy, defense and related materiel, manufacturing, marine, metals and mining, financial services, security, or technology sector of the Cuban economy, as identified in and determined pursuant to E.O. 14404—are themselves at risk of sanctions.  Non-U.S. persons, including foreign financial institutions, should proceed with caution in any dealings with a party sanctioned under this authority.  Actions to return assets to a sanctioned party or transfer them to another jurisdiction for potential use by the target expose non-U.S. persons to significant sanctions risk.  All property and interests in property of persons that are blocked pursuant to the Cuban Assets Control Regulations (CACR) continue to be blocked.  The CACR prohibits persons subject to U.S. jurisdiction from dealing in property in which Cuba or a Cuban national has an interest, unless authorized or exempt. 

The power and integrity of U.S. government sanctions derive not only from the U.S. government’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.    

Petitions for removal from the SDN List may be routed through OFAC’s Reconsiderations Portal.  Petitioners may also refer to the Department of State’s Delisting Guidance page.

Fact Sheet

item.title: U.S. Sanctions Fraudulent Ship Registries and Aviation Support for Iranian Regime
item.dc:creator: Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
item.description:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman

U.S. Sanctions Fraudulent Ship Registries and Aviation Support for Iranian Regime

Press Statement

November 4, 2026

Today, the United States is acting against a criminal network that sells fraudulent flags to the Iranian regime’s shadow fleet of ships.  The United States is also targeting a Türkiye-based company that provides ground services to sanctioned Iranian airlines.  The Department of the Treasury is taking these actions under Operation Economic Outcast, the Trump Administration’s campaign to cut off revenue the Iranian regime uses to fund terrorism, weapons proliferation, and its proxies across the Middle East.

For more than a decade, India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, have formed companies that pose as the flag registries and maritime service providers of countries and jurisdictions such as Guyana, Eswatini, Aruba, Mali, Mozambique, Malawi, Sint Maarten, and Timor-Leste.  These companies have sold fraudulent registrations and certificates to vessels carrying illicit Iranian oil. Most of these governments have publicly disavowed the fraudulent registries.

Today’s action targets 13 individuals and companies in the Sharma network.  We commend the governments that have exposed these schemes.  We call on flag states, port authorities, and the maritime industry to verify vessel registrations and deny shadow fleet vessels access to their waters and ports.

The designations imposed today are being taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian petroleum, petrochemical, and aviation sectors, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. For more information on today’s action, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.

item.title: Joint Statement on the 53rd U.S.-Portugal Standing Bilateral Commission
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesman
item.description:
Office of the Spokesman

Joint Statement on the 53rd U.S.-Portugal Standing Bilateral Commission

Media Note

November 3, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and the Republic of Portugal on the occasion of the 53rd meeting of the U.S.-Portugal Standing Bilateral Commission.

Begin Text:

The Governments of the United States of America and the Portuguese Republic convened the 53rd meeting of the Portugal-United States Standing Bilateral Commission (SBC). The dialogue focused on the following priorities:

Defense and Security Cooperation: The delegations reaffirmed NATO’s central role in Euro-Atlantic security and their shared commitment to allied defense investment in line with commitments made at the 2025 NATO Summit in The Hague. Recognizing the strong bilateral defense relationship and the successful collaboration on defense equipment programmes, both sides welcome the continued expansion of cooperation between their respective armed forces. They highlighted the ongoing implementation of the State Partnership Program between Portugal and the Illinois National Guard, including activities already underway and further engagements planned to strengthen interoperability, readiness, and the exchange of expertise.

Cooperation in the Azores/Lajes: Both sides praised the growing U.S. engagement with the Autonomous Region of the Azores. The delegations committed to expanding economic opportunity and people-to-people ties that benefit Azorean communities. The delegations acknowledged the U.S. Air Force’s efforts in environmental remediation.

Economic security/CEO Forum: The delegations reaffirmed their strong commitment to reinforcing economic ties between Portugal and the United States. Building on the 52nd SBC meeting commitments and the October 8 meeting between Secretary Rubio and Foreign Minister Rangel in Lisbon, the two governments confirmed the inaugural CEO Forum Plenary Meeting to be held on November 10, 2026, in Lisbon. With this initiative, both sides aim to identify new opportunities for trade and investment, while facilitating job creation and promoting economic growth and security, to the benefit of both the United States and Portugal.

The United States congratulated Portugal on its election to the UN Security Council for the 2027-2028 term. Both delegations agreed to cooperate within the Council to address the pressing topics of the global agenda.

The delegations reaffirmed their sustained interest in continuing and deepening the bilateral strategic partnership.

The 54th SBC will meet in Lisbon, in 2027.

End Text.
